newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up in sluggish trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended slightly up on Monday mainly because of institutional support buying in market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, brokers said.
But trading was dull with volume only half of the average level due to most investors taking a wait-and-see attitude after sharp falls on Friday, they said.
The B index inched up 0.521 points or 0.62 percent to 84.959 points on thin volume of 11.024 million shares worth $7.711 million.
"Market sentiment has been hurt by the government's recent clampdown, but some institutions which hold large positions in Lujiazui still tried to push its price up," said one broker.
"With trading volume so thin, upward potential will be limited," another broker said. "Investor concerns about possible further crackdown measures may pull the index down again."
Of 43 B shares, 39 traded, with 16 up, eight flat and 15 down.
Shanghai Kaikai Industrial Co was the star on a technical rebound, jumping $0.036 or 8.69 percent to $0.450 on volume of 327,000 shares.
Lujiazui was the most actively traded on institutional support, up $0.054 or 3.86 percent to $1.450 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index closed up also on a technical rebound, but trading was dull and the mood cautious, brokers said.
The index gained 30.562 points or 2.22 percent to 1,406.472 points on volume of 529.1 million shares worth 6.8 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index jumped 135.703 points or 3.58 percent to 3,922.289 points.

China Sichuan International Co was the top gainer on talk of local government support to help it recover from 1996 losses, surging 0.74 yuan or 10.02 percent to 8.12 yuan on volume of 3.3 million shares.
